# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

```
Supported sub-commands:
	check - run linter over specified targets
		$ go-critic check -help
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='paramTypeCombine,unslice' strings bytes
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./...
	version - print linter version
		$ go-critic version
	doc - get installed checkers documentation
		$ go-critic doc -help
		$ go-critic doc
		$ go-critic doc checkerName
```

### Examples

```bash
# Runs all stable checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check fmt

# Run all stable checkers on `pkg1` and `pkg2`
go-critic check pkg1 pkg2

# Run all stable checkers on `fmt` package and configure rangeExprCopy checker
go-critic check -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold 128 fmt

# Runs specified checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check -enable elseif,paramName fmt

# Run all stable checkers on current dir and all its children recursively:
go-critic check ./...

# Like above, but without `appendAssign` check:
go-critic check -disable=appendAssign ./...

# Run all stable checkers on `foo.go` file:
go-critic check foo.go

# Run stable diagnostics over `strings` package:
go-critic check -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental' strings

# Run all stable and non-opinionated checks:
go-critic check -enableAll -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./src/...
```

> To get a list of available checker parameters, run `go-critic doc <checkerName>`.

### Checker Tags

In place of a single name, **tag** can be used. Tag is a named checkers group.

Tags:

* `#diagnostic` - kind of checks that detect various errors in code
* `#style` - kind of checks that find style issues in code
* `#performance` - kind of checks that detect potential performance issues in code
* `#experimental` - check is under testing and development. Disabled by default
* `#opinionated` - check can be unwanted for some people. Disabled by default
* `#security` - kind of checks that find security issues in code. Disabled by default

## Documentation

For complete documentation and a full list of checkers, visit [go-critic.com](https://go-critic.com/overview).

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

```
Supported sub-commands:
	check - run linter over specified targets
		$ go-critic check -help
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='paramTypeCombine,unslice' strings bytes
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./...
	version - print linter version
		$ go-critic version
	doc - get installed checkers documentation
		$ go-critic doc -help
		$ go-critic doc
		$ go-critic doc checkerName
```

### Examples

```bash
# Runs all stable checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check fmt

# Run all stable checkers on `pkg1` and `pkg2`
go-critic check pkg1 pkg2

# Run all stable checkers on `fmt` package and configure rangeExprCopy checker
go-critic check -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold 128 fmt

# Runs specified checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check -enable elseif,paramName fmt

# Run all stable checkers on current dir and all its children recursively:
go-critic check ./...

# Like above, but without `appendAssign` check:
go-critic check -disable=appendAssign ./...

# Run all stable checkers on `foo.go` file:
go-critic check foo.go

# Run stable diagnostics over `strings` package:
go-critic check -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental' strings

# Run all stable and non-opinionated checks:
go-critic check -enableAll -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./src/...
```

> To get a list of available checker parameters, run `go-critic doc <checkerName>`.

### Checker Tags

In place of a single name, **tag** can be used. Tag is a named checkers group.

Suggests to use pointer to array to avoid the copy using `&` on range expression.

}

var xs [2048]byte

	// Loop body.

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

default_checkers = "appendAssign,argOrder,assignOp,badCall,badCond,captLocal,caseOrder,codegenComment,commentFormatting,defaultCaseOrder,deprecatedComment,dupArg,dupBranchBody,dupCase,dupSubExpr,elseif,exitAfterDefer,flagDeref,flagName,ifElseChain,mapKey,newDeref,offBy1,regexpMust,singleCaseSwitch,sloppyLen,sloppyTypeAssert,switchTrue,typeSwitchVar,underef,unlambda,unslice,valSwap,wrapperFunc".split(',')

out_lines = []
for checker in default_checkers:
    doc_path = docs_dir / f"{checker}.txt"
    if not doc_path.exists():
        print(f"missing {checker}")
        continue
    txt = doc_path.read_text()
    # Extract Non-compliant code block
    # Pattern: Non-compliant code:\n<code>\n\nCompliant code:
    m = re.search(r'Non-compliant code:\n(.*?)\n\nCompliant code:', txt, re.S)
    if not m:
        print(f"no snippet for {checker}")
        continue
    snippet = m.group(1).strip()
    # Remove leading spaces? snack contains code lines
    # Build file
    # Ensure package header
    code = snippet
    # If snippet doesn't start with package, wrap
    if not code.strip().startswith("package"):
        # Add package and maybe imports
        # Detect if snippet contains import or package
        # Wrap with package p and maybe function
        # If snippet looks like function or snippet without func, we need to wrap differently
        # Simplify: create file with package p and snippet inside func
        # For many checkers, snippet is not full file, we need to embed
        # Try to create a file that includes snippet as is with package line if not present
        if "func" not in code and "var" not in code and "import" not in code and "type" not in code:
            # snippet maybe expression like `x = x * 2` - need function
            code = f"package p\nfunc foo() {{\n{code}\n}}\n"
        else:
            # include snippet with package header if missing
            code = f"package p\n{code}\n" if not code.lstrip().startswith("package") else code
            # Ensure imports if needed for checker like wrapperFunc needs imports?
        # Clean
    else:
        code = code + "\n"
    # Write to temp
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        td_path = pathlib.Path(td)
        # Need go.mod
        (td_path / "go.mod").write_text("module p\ngo 1.21\n")
        # Write file
        f_path = td_path / "x.go"
        f_path.write_text(code)
        # Run check
        cmd = ["/workspace/executable", "check", f"-enable={checker}", str(f_path)]
        # Also need to handle -checkTests etc not needed
        result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=str(td_path))
        out = result.stderr.strip() + result.stdout.strip()
        # Also try with directory pattern
        # Use same cmd but with package dir
        # For debugging, capture snippet
        print(f"== {checker} ==")
        print(code[:400].replace("\n","\\n"))
        print("--- output ---")
        print(out[:500])
        print("exit", result.returncode)
        print()
        out_lines.append((checker, out, code))

The commands are:

    check             run linter over specified targets
    doc               get installed checkers documentation
    help              shows help message
    version           shows version of the application

Version: v0.0.0-SNAPSHOT
"""

# For unknown command: need to check format:  "\"<cmd>\" unknown command\nRun \"go-critic help\" for usage.\n" stdout, and "no such command \"<cmd>\"\n" stderr
# For did-you-mean: "\"<cmd>\" unknown command, did you mean \"<suggestion>\"?\nRun \"go-critic help\" for usage.\n" stdout, "no such command \"<cmd>\"\n" stderr
# Need to determine which commands trigger did-you-mean.
# Observed:

# chek -> did you mean "check"
# versin -> did you mean "version"
# docc -> did you mean "doc"
# versiona -> did you mean "version"
# But -h, -?, -v, --unknown, unknown, foobar -> no did-you-mean
# Let's test more:

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

	}
}

func run(args []string) error {
	if len(args) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "no args provided")
		return nil
	}
	cmd := args[0]
	rest := args[1:]
	switch cmd {
	case "help":
		// help ignores extra args and flags
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, usageText)
		// help prints newline after? usageText already has newline
		// original help output ends with extra newline? Let's check: help ends with "\n\n"? Actually usageText ends with "\n\n"? We defined with final newline.
		// In observed, help stdout ends with "\n\n"? Our usageText ends with "Version: v0.0.0-SNAPSHOT\n\n" ??? Check cat: help output had blank line after?
		// Let's ensure exactly.
		return nil
	case "version":
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "go-critic version: "+version)
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "")
		return nil
	case "doc":
		return runDoc(rest)
	case "check":
		return runCheck(rest)
	default:
		// unknown command handling with suggestion
		suggestion := suggestCommand(cmd)
		if suggestion != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "\"%s\" unknown command, did you mean \"%s\"?\n", cmd, suggestion)
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "Run \"go-critic help\" for usage.")
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "")
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "\"%s\" unknown command\n", cmd)
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "Run \"go-critic help\" for usage.")
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "")
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "no such command \"%s\"\n", cmd)
		return nil
	}
}

func suggestCommand(cmd string) string {
	candidates := []string{"check", "doc", "help", "version"}
	best := ""
	bestDist := 100
	for _, c := range candidates {
		d := levenshtein(cmd, c)
		if d < bestDist {
			bestDist = d
			best = c
		}
	}
	if bestDist <= 2 {
		return best
	}
	return ""
}

func levenshtein(a, b string) int {
	m := len(a)
	n := len(b)
	dp := make([][]int, m+1)
	for i := range dp {
		dp[i] = make([]int, n+1)
	}
	for i := 0; i <= m; i++ {
		dp[i][0] = i
	}
	for j := 0; j <= n; j++ {
		dp[0][j] = j
	}
	for i := 1; i <= m; i++ {
		for j := 1; j <= n; j++ {
			cost := 0
			if a[i-1] != b[j-1] {
				cost = 1
			}
			dp[i][j] = min(dp[i-1][j]+1, dp[i][j-1]+1, dp[i-1][j-1]+cost)
		}
	}
	return dp[m][n]
}
func min(a, b, c int) int {
	if a < b {
		if a < c {
			return a
		}
		return c
	}
	if b < c {
		return b
	}
	return c
}

#!/bin/bash
# Test a wide range of behaviors to ensure replica matches
set +e

run_and_diff() {
  desc="$1"
  shift
  orig_cmd="$1"
  shift
  replica_cmd="$1"
  shift
  echo "=== $desc ==="
  ${orig_cmd} > /tmp/orig.txt 2> /tmp/orig_err.txt; orig_rc=$?
  ${replica_cmd} > /tmp/replica.txt 2> /tmp/replica_err.txt; replica_rc=$?
  if [ "$orig_rc" != "$replica_rc" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: exit code orig $orig_rc replica $replica_rc"
  else
    echo "OK exit $orig_rc"
  fi
  if ! diff -q /tmp/orig.txt /tmp/replica.txt > /dev/null; then
    echo "FAIL stdout diff"
    diff -u /tmp/orig.txt /tmp/replica.txt | head -n 20
  else
    echo "OK stdout"
  fi
  if ! diff -q /tmp/orig_err.txt /tmp/replica_err.txt > /dev/null; then
    echo "FAIL stderr diff"
    diff -u /tmp/orig_err.txt /tmp/replica_err.txt | head -n 50
  else
    echo "OK stderr"
  fi
  echo ""
}

run_and_diff "help" "./executable help" "/tmp/replica_exe help"
run_and_diff "help extra" "./executable help extra" "/tmp/replica_exe help extra"

cat > /tmp/run_final_comprehensive.sh <<'EOS'
#!/bin/bash
set +e
fail=0
pass=0
check() {
  desc="$1"
  orig_cmd="$2"
  replica_cmd="$3"
  # run orig
  bash -c "$orig_cmd" > /tmp/orig.txt 2> /tmp/orig_err.txt; orig_rc=$?
  bash -c "$replica_cmd" > /tmp/replica.txt 2> /tmp/replica_err.txt; replica_rc=$?
  if [ "$orig_rc" != "$replica_rc" ]; then
    echo "FAIL $desc: exit orig $orig_rc replica $replica_rc"
    fail=$((fail+1))
    return
  fi
  if ! diff -q /tmp/orig.txt /tmp/replica.txt > /dev/null; then
    echo "FAIL $desc: stdout diff"
    diff -u /tmp/orig.txt /tmp/replica.txt | head -n 20
    fail=$((fail+1))
    return
  fi
  if ! diff -q /tmp/orig_err.txt /tmp/replica_err.txt > /dev/null; then
    echo "FAIL $desc: stderr diff"
    diff -u /tmp/orig_err.txt /tmp/replica_err.txt | head -n 50
    fail=$((fail+1))
    return
  fi
  echo "PASS $desc"
  pass=$((pass+1))
}

#!/bin/bash
set +e
fail=0
pass=0
check() {
  desc="$1"
  orig_cmd="$2"
  replica_cmd="$3"
  bash -c "$orig_cmd" > /tmp/orig.txt 2> /tmp/orig_err.txt; orig_rc=$?
  bash -c "$replica_cmd" > /tmp/replica.txt 2> /tmp/replica_err.txt; replica_rc=$?
  # Filter go invalid addresses
  grep -v "0xc" /tmp/orig_err.txt > /tmp/orig_f.txt 2>/dev/null || cp /tmp/orig_err.txt /tmp/orig_f.txt
  grep -v "0xc" /tmp/replica_err.txt > /tmp/replica_f.txt 2>/dev/null || cp /tmp/replica_err.txt /tmp/replica_f.txt
  if [ "$orig_rc" != "$replica_rc" ]; then
    echo "FAIL $desc: exit orig $orig_rc replica $replica_rc"
    fail=$((fail+1))
    return
  fi
  if ! diff -q /tmp/orig.txt /tmp/replica.txt > /dev/null; then
    echo "FAIL $desc: stdout diff"
    fail=$((fail+1))
    return
  fi
  if ! diff -q /tmp/orig_f.txt /tmp/replica_f.txt > /dev/null; then
    echo "FAIL $desc: stderr diff"
    fail=$((fail+1))
    return
  fi
  echo "PASS $desc"
  pass=$((pass+1))
}

check "help extra" "./executable help extra" "/tmp/replica_exe help extra"
